title: Embedded Feature Deprecation and Migration Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

SUMMARY
This playbook defines the product, operational, and commercial approach for deprecating embedded feature variants (lightweight local runtimes, deprecated compact quantized variants, or SKU-level embedded features) and migrating affected customers to supported alternatives. It covers the end-to-end process: criteria for deprecation, technical migration paths, pricing/credits policy, communication templates, monitoring and rollback, and post-sunset validation.

INTENDED AUDIENCE
- Product managers and PMMs owning embedded/edge features
- Engineering leads for runtime, SDKs, and inference systems
- Customer Success & Sales teams responsible for migrations
- Legal and Finance for contract/credit handling
- Support and SRE oncall engineers

Why this playbook exists
- Reduce fragmentation of supported runtimes and improve engineering velocity by consolidating variants
- Ensure predictable customer experience and cost signals during migrations
- Protect SLOs and quality by moving customers to variants with ongoing validation and security patches

Goals (measurable)
1) Complete migration of 90% of eligible customers from deprecated embedded variant A to recommended variant B within 180 days of public announcement.
2) Keep defect regression rate <1% during migration window as measured by pre/post eval suites.
3) Issue pro-rated credits or migration assistance to impacted customers within 30 days of migration kickoff where contractually required.

Non-Goals
- This playbook does not redefine model-level safety or content policy (handled by Safety team).
- It does not cover migration between hosted and private control plane modalities (see hosted-to-dedicated transition playbook).

Context and Definitions
- Embedded feature: a runtime or SDK feature that customers deploy within their environment or bundling (edge SDK, embedded quantized runtime, on-device adapter).
- Deprecated variant: the specific variant we plan to deprecate (e.g., compact-quant-v2).
- Recommended variant: the supported alternative (e.g., compact-v3 or hosted fallback profile).

Requirements (product + acceptance)
- RQ-01: Migration Pathing
  - Every deprecated public API or SDK surface must have at least one documented migration path with code examples.
  - Acceptance: migration doc validated by engineering runbook and cross-team signoff.
- RQ-02: Automated Compatibility Detector
  - Provide an offline tool (cli) to scan customer manifests and suggest replacements and impact (latency/cost delta).
  - Acceptance: tool correctly identifies 95% of variant usages in a curated sample of 200 manifests.
- RQ-03: Backwards-safe Fallback
  - Implement server-side compatibility fallback for 90 days post-deprecation announcement for non-API-breaking calls where possible.
  - Acceptance: fallback has an observability dashboard and anomaly alerting tied to SLOs.
- RQ-04: Billing & Credits
  - Define crediting rules, pro-ration algorithm, and Finance approval workflow.
  - Acceptance: one end-to-end migration invoice test executed in staging.
- RQ-05: Customer Observability
  - Add migration-specific metrics: migration_progress, migration_errors, migration_time_estimate, fidelity_regression_rate.
  - Acceptance: dashboards and alerts created in Console and validated by customer success.

Design constraints and guardrails
- Do not introduce client-side breaking changes without a one major-minor deprecation announcement cadence (minimum 60 days).
- Maintain one canonical migration path per major customer segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise).
- Preserve token accounting and billing semantics: users on committed capacity should not see unexpected overages due to migration.

Proposed Technical Design
1) Migration helper CLI (embed-migrate)
   - A python-based tool distributed via pip and as a Docker image.
   - Core commands: analyze, plan, apply, rollback, report.

   Example: analyze output (JSON)
   ```json
   {
     "customer_id": "acct_123",
     "deprecated_variant_usage": ["compact-quant-v2"],
     "recommended_replacement": "compact-v3",
     "estimated_latency_change_ms": 18,
     "estimated_cost_delta_pct": 12
   }
   ```

2) Automated migration APIs
   - POST /v1/migrations/plan -> returns plan-id
   - POST /v1/migrations/plan/{id}/apply -> begins staged rollout

   Sample cURL to create a plan:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/migrations/plan -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"t-789","variants":[{"from":"compact-quant-v2","to":"compact-v3"}],"risk_profile":"conservative"}'
   ```

3) Fallback routing policy
   - Introduce a migration-specific routing rule: if client requests deprecated variant and migration window active, route to recommended variant with header X-Migration-Proxy: true.
   - The proxy must attach migration metadata for traceability (migration-plan-id, step).

Migration phases and playbook steps
- PREANNOUNCEMENT (internal) — Owners: Product, Eng-runtime, Legal
  1) Finalize sunset date and timeline.
  2) Create migration CLI MVP and run identification on internal corp manifests.
  3) Review contract implications with Finance & Legal.
  4) Prepare support KB and self-serve migration docs.

- ANNOUNCEMENT — Owners: PMM, Customer Success, Sales
  1) Publish deprecation notice (60 days min) to Console Notices and email to active tenants using variant.
  2) Open lift tickets for high-risk enterprise accounts and schedule migration calls.
  3) Provide migration credits & hands-on assistance guidelines.

- MIGRATION WINDOW (60–180 days) — Owners: Customer Success, Eng-runtime, SRE
  1) Run automated analysis for enrolled customers.
  2) Offer opt-in auto-migration with a conservative rollback window (7 days).
  3) Monitor fidelity_regression_rate and open immediate rollback on regressions >1%.
  4) Apply billing adjustments and record credits in migration ledger.

- POST-SUNSET (> 180 days) — Owners: Product, Legal, Finance, Support
  1) Terminate public access to deprecated variant (hard cut).
  2) Complete pro-rated credits and close migration tickets.
  3) Run final audit and publish migration retros and metrics.

Rollout timeline (example)
| Phase | Duration | Key deliverable | Owner |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Internal prep | 30 days | CLI v0.5 + contract checklist | Eng & Product |
| Public announcement | 60 days | Notice + playbook | PMM & CS |
| Opt-in migrations | 90 days | 70% of SMB + 50% of enterprise auto-plans | CS & Eng |
| Hard sunsetting | 1 day | Variant disabled | Eng-runtime |

Pricing and packaging impact
- Principles
  - Do not bill customers for dual-use during covered migration windows beyond agreed contract terms.
  - Provide migration credits when a migration causes >10% cost increase for an enterprise customer within the first billing cycle.

- Example credit rules
  - Rule C1: If estimated_cost_delta_pct > 15% and customer is on committed capacity -> issue credit equal to 50% of the delta for first 30 days (Finance approval required).
  - Rule C2: For self-serve customers affected with >25% delta -> offer a 30-day temporary promo code for new variant.

- Billing workflow (summary)
  1) Migration plan created -> system calculates estimated delta and flags possible credits.
  2) Finance reviews high-cost cases and approves crediting.
  3) Credits applied and visible on customer billing page.

Operational runbook (SRE & Support)
- Key dashboards to create
  - migrations.active-plans (per-tenant)
  - migrations.errors (by error-code)
  - migration-fidelity-regressions (per-tenant, per-prompt-set)
  - fallback-proxy-rate (requests/s)

- Incident play (example)
  1) Alert: migration-fidelity-regressions > 1% across >5 tenants for 15 mins.
  2) Action: Pause auto-migrations (API: POST /v1/migrations/controls/pause) and open migration-incident channel.
  3) Rollback plan: trigger rollback via plan API and notify CS.
  4) Postmortem: 72-hour RCA and update playbook.

Customer communications (templates)
- Announcement subject line: "Action required: Upcoming change to your embedded runtime (compact-quant-v2) — migration options"
- Key message pillars:
  - What is changing and why (concise)
  - What you need to do (options: self-migrate, schedule assist, opt-in auto-migrate)
  - Dates and impact on billing
  - Where to get help (CS contact, docs link, migration CLI)

Sample support KB table of contents
1. Overview and rationale
2. How to detect if you are impacted (CLI example)
3. Migration options (self-serve, assisted, hybrid)
4. Billing implications and credits
5. Troubleshooting common regressions
6. Rollback instructions

Release notes template (for SDK/runtime releases associated with migration)
- Version: 1.2.0-migrate
- Highlights: Adds migration plan API, improves fallback proxy header, provides cost estimator.
- Migration notes: Run `embed-migrate analyze` and review recommended replacements.
- Breaking changes: None (if present, list and include mitigation steps).

Metrics and SLOs to track success
- Adoption metrics: % tenants migrated, mean time to migrate per tenant (days).
- Quality metrics: fidelity_regression_rate (target <1%), post-migration error rate delta (target <0.5%).
- Commercial metrics: total credits issued (USD), migration-related churn (target 0%).

Post-migration validation checklist (per-tenant)
1) Run canonical pre/post eval harness on customer prompt set.
2) Verify latency and throughput within agreed delta.
3) Confirm billing statement adjusted as expected.
4) CS sign-off: customer confirms feature parity or acceptable fidelity.

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: Unexpected fidelity drop at scale -> Mitigation: Canary to 5% of production traffic and run prompt-set A/B for 48 hours.
- Risk: Billing disputes -> Mitigation: Grace period credits and transparent cost estimator in plan report.
- Risk: Automation bugs -> Mitigation: Manual gate for enterprise tenants and runbook rehearsals.

Ownership and contacts

- Eng runtime lead: Miguel Ramos (eng-serving-runtime)
- CS lead: Claire Nguyen (customer-success)
- Finance contact: Jordan Liu (finance-legal)
- Oncall SRE: see eng-sre rota in Runbooks space

Appendices
A. Example migration CLI commands
```bash
# analyze customer manifest
embed-migrate analyze --manifest ./manifests/customer-123.yml --output ./analysis.json

# create remote plan
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/migrations/plan -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"t-789","variants":[{"from":"compact-quant-v2","to":"compact-v3"}],"risk_profile":"conservative"}'

# apply plan
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/migrations/plan/plan-456/apply -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

B. Example audit CSV columns
- tenant_id, plan_id, start_ts, end_ts, from_variant, to_variant, estimated_cost_delta_pct, credits_issued_usd, post_migration_fidelity_delta_pct

C. Postmortem template pointers
- timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, follow-ups, owner sign-offs

End of playbook
